item.content:encoded:
What ‘free basics’ ideally seeks
1. Digital equity
2. Access to education, jobs, news etc. for billion Indians

On digging through facebook’s developer guide I found the following.
1. Facebook’s free basics supports both smart phones and feature phones (read those small screen phones which have virtually unusable browsers)
2. Websites need to be developed in such a way that feature phones are supported, yeah well lets go back to 90s
3. All the traffic will be routed through internet.org servers so that ISPs can zero rate your service
4. Facebook can truncate videos, images. Basically morph your site. Read stalking, censorship.

Now considering what they are offering and what they want in return the scales are not equal. Free basics is just a medium to get more people online and familiar with Facebook and off course in turn Facebook knows them literally. None of the already shady government sites would work on free basics, talk about fucking digital equity. Free basics is canabalizing the internet and so will others bigshots given a free hand. Forget open standards, open sources. I don’t subscribe to the notion “something is better than nothing” there are always costs, costs we are not aware of and that is even worse.

item.content:encoded:
Pondicherry is a union territory of India with the city of Pondicherry as its capital. The city fondly called Pondy is a coastal city with a mix of different ethnicities, architectures. The city is well planned and some of its areas are simply mesmerizing in terms of its beauty. I visited the place recently with a friend of mine.

We started our journey to Pondicherry from Bangalore on the night of 31st July 2015. The bus journey started around 2300Hrs in the night and ended 8 hours later in the morning around 0730Hrs. took an auto rickshaw to a place called New Guest House. The guest house is a religious place so you aren’t allowed to drink or smoke and need to be back before 2230Hrs in the night. If that’s fine with you then it’s the place of your stay in Pondicherry for several reasons. First it’s just 50mtrs away from the promenade beach and at the edge of the most famous white town area of Pondy. Secondly it’s pretty cheap considering the locality as it costs only 400 rupees for a single night stay, and being affiliated to religious organization it’s neat and tidy. We checked in, got refreshed and came out on the promenade beach for a refreshingly beautiful morning walk. Beaches are the most serene places to be at in the mornings.

We had a breakfast at a road side joint, the street food in Pondy is quite cheaper and won’t burn into your pockets. We decided to take an auto to a place called Paradise beach also famously called Boat House. The autos in Pondy don’t make use of the meters and the drivers will let you know the fare firsthand. The self-fixed prices of the autos are quite steep and will remain so even after a hard bargain, sometimes you can’t even bargain. Alternately the public transport in Pondicherry is almost free, it costs you just 5 rupees from any place to place. So make it a point to lookout for public buses or ask around. Sometime you won’t have a choice and would need to use the auto.

Paradise beach is sort of an island beach and requires a boat ride to reach. The beach is clean, no litter in the vicinity with lots of photogenic spaces.


We visited a place called Arikamedu in the afternoon, it used to be a Roman trading hub in the ancient times. There is not much to see there and you should visit only if you are a true history enthusiast. In this part of the Pondy you will find simple Tamil style homes and is a part of Pondy that is often less talked of.

Relics from the first century

We were back to the guest house by late afternoon and decided to explore Pondy markets after a brief rest. We had some street food at Chinna Kadai market, then walked from street to street. There are specialized streets in the city, they give you a glimpse into the planning of the city. One should explore all the streets around MG road area like Nehru Street, Mission Street and many others. Also give a visit to Arulmigu Manakula temple. There are also quite a many churches in the city. You can also find Aurobindo Ashram near the same area. The city looks pretty amazing in the night. The walk along the Promenade beach in the night will make you spellbound, the French windows just look majestic at night. Sit for some long time at the beach and listen to the sound of the waves and observe the people around.

We checked out the next day from the guest house. Took a bus to the New city bus stand from the market near Pondicherry railway station. Got into another bus towards Auroville. The bus drops you at the main road leading to Auroville, however the places to visit in Auroville are about 8kms from there. Through some miscalculation we didn’t take an auto rickshaw to the Auroville town and ended up walking 8kms.

Auroville is an experimental township, it’s an international community undivided by ideas of nationality, religion or ethnicity. Since we walked our way we got to see the place in all its glory. The place is one big man made forest. The architecture of the place is awe inspiring and will make you promise yourself that you will come back for more number of days to stay here.

Took an auto from the Auroville back to the main road, visited Auroville beach a walkable distance from there. Had some fun at the beach, there were few absolutely drunk college students at the beach and had an opportunity to photograph one.

Back from the beach and back to the city bus stand, we visited Pondicherry botanical garden, it’s more of a park that botanical garden. We spent last few hours in the city at the Promenade beach. I had some really creative thoughts emerging in my mind as I stared at the endless ocean.

Pondicherry is a city to visit, for its architecture, for its culture and for its simplicity. It’s not a perfect city and there is a lot that its people and infrastructure can improve upon. I found one thing very disturbing, the chief minister of the territory was on an image making spree in the city. There were these huge poster of Mr. N. Rangaswamy flanking every corner of the city. However amusing the posters might be, the sight was plain ugly. On another aspect the city has a lot of open sewers, the smaller sewers should be covered at the very least. However I liked the fact that people were quite laid back and didn’t seem to be in a lot of hurry like in the cities of Mumbai, Pune or Bangalore.

item.title: Trek to Kunti Betta, Karnataka
item.description: There is something about trekking that enlivens your senses, releases the tensions within; both physical and mental. It’s an ordeal into achieving nothing. item.content:encoded:
There is something about trekking that enlivens your senses, releases the tensions within; both physical and mental. It’s an ordeal into achieving nothing. Many of my friends find it hard to follow the reasons why I trek. I hardly care about the summit or the destination. For me the journey itself holds the charm above all else. Okay so all philosophy apart, I write this blog post to share my experiences of travelling to a place called Kunti Betta 100 km away from Bangalore.

Woke up at 0445 hours on the sunday, 26th July 15. Being the organizer had to call 7 more people to make sure they were awake. We were suppose to leave the hostel by 0530 hours, but somehow someone will always find some excuse to get you late. 🙂 So we started 20 minutes late. Reached Hosa Road Junction by 0600 Hours and reached the Majestic Bus station at 0640 hours. We had to hurry to the adjacent railway station almost running en route. Got the tickets and boarded the train bound for Mysore at 0700 hours. Our destination was Pandavpura, the place is believed to have been the stay of the Pandav from Mahabharata during their exile.

Train to Pandavpura

The morning train journey was surreal, the smoky train engine kept me interested until the end. We reached the place around 0930 hours. Walked out of the railway station and searched for a place to have breakfast. Pandavpura town is about 4 km away from the railway station. If you wish to have your breakfast at a neat and clean place then area near the station is not a place for you. We looked out for a place to eat but no eating joint matched our idea of a good place. Finally we settled for one less shady looking joint and asked for breakfast options. The place served Rice(Pulav), idly, udid-vada and puri. The prices of the menu-items were way to cheap. We ordered 3 rice plates, 2 idli-vada plates and started eating. The food was so freaking awesome and tasty we ended up eating like 6 rice plates, 4 idli-vada plates, 1 Puri-sabji. And to add to our delight we paid only 220 rupees for all that food. Sometimes unfamiliar and not so good looking places have the best things to offer. :D.

We negotiated with an ambassador taxi driver to take us to Kunti betta, 8 of us squeezed ourselves in the royal ambassador and drove off for Kunti Betta. The photos below will describe the beauty of the place and I would let you imagine the words. Just to mention, the place might get tricky to climb if it rains, that’s all.

After climbing down we started off for Tonnur lake some 15km away. The lake is super clean, we reached from the point where people enter the lake for a swim. Had lots of photos taken; diving, jumping and shouting. We met with another travelling group from Karnataka at the lake. The guys spoke broken Hindi and English, but somehow we got along very well. They offered us delicious chicken and rice to eat. They really liked the fact that 8 of us came from 7 different states in India. After a final photograph with them we headed back to Pandavpura railway station. We just made it in time for 1350 hours train back to Bangalore. There were no seats available so had to squeeze ourselves onto the upper birth where one couldn’t sit with his head and spine erect. After one and half hour of acrobatics on the upper birth where I also managed to get some decent amount sleep, I got down and spent the rest of the time at the train door – my most favorite spot in any train.

Watched the railway track side ghettos of Bangalore while getting back felt a bit sad as to why people are forced to abandon clean environments of the villages to settle in such stinking, sunlight deprived places and to what avail? item.title: Chavand, Shivneri Trek
item.description: The monsoon has been delayed this year, however the weather seems much cooler now in comparison to summer. Perfect time to come out of trekking hibernation. item.content:encoded:
The monsoon has been delayed this year, however the weather seems much cooler now in comparison to summer. Perfect time to come out of trekking hibernation. Last Saturday we planned a trek to Chavand and Shivneri, two hill forts situated in Pune district. We started early morning around 6am from Pune and reached the destination around 7:45 am. Had a breakfast of tasty Misal at a small roadside hotel. 

The base village of Chavand is a quiet and beautiful place. The houses in village are traditional with roofs mainly of roof tiles and metal sheets. There is a single main road that passes through the entire village to end of which there is a primary school. We parked our car in the primary school playground. Filled our water bottles and asked locals for directions to the fort and places of interest to be seen atop the fort.

The climb to the fort is not a difficult one, currently work is in progress for creating steps all the way to the top. The fort itself is a simple plateau without huge walls and big bastions. What’s more remarkable about the place is the restoration effort carried out by government with assistance from locals. It’s clear from one look that all money spent here in maintenance hasn’t been a waste. Although not a major tourist attraction still, there are enough sign boards in place. Most requesting tourist to maintain the sanctity of the place. There are thousands of tree saplings planted and cared for, in a few years’ time, visit to this place will be more of ecological one than archaeological. We all have a lot to learn from the simple village folks here, primarily heritage and forest conservation. There are remains of ancient Shiva temple on the fort which reminds you of the wonderful ancient art and architecture. To me it seemed straight out of an Indiana jones movie 🙂 .

The sky looked amazing with dark rainy clouds, however we missed the most anticipated rain. It would have been an icing on the cake. Having strolled around for some time, we descended the fort. At the foot of the fort met some village children who had picked two small plastic bagful of jambul (Java plum) fruits. They wished to sell those, shyly one asked if we would buy? We happily bought all the fruits they had, they would have given us the entire fetch for whatever we were ready to pay, but we decided to stick to our morals and give them a fair return. Back to our car, played bit of cricket with village children. Got refreshed at a well nearby drawing water using a bucket tied to rope. Once freshened up we started back to the fort Shivneri. It’s hardly a 20-30 min drive from Chavand.

Shivneri is birthplace of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the founder of Maratha Empire. The place holds a good deal of reverence in my heart. It’s heartening to see lots of restoration work underway on this fort. However call me a skeptic but I do not fully appreciate the nature of restoration work carried out around most forts in Maharashtra. Restoration workers either have no idea of the aesthetic value of the place they are restoring or they are hardly bothered. The same is the case with contractors who are hired to do the job. Archaeological survey teams who can actually make justice to the restoration process are poorly numbered and cannot supervise every small activity. Still even use of simple common sense, and an effort at letting the originality shine and the patchwork be there to support the beauty and not obstruct it will make a great difference.

Like Pratapgad, Shivneri isn’t much of a trek but a long walk. Many beautiful structures still remain intact thanks to restoration work. There are enough spots for lots of photography. Green cover too on the fort is excellent and provides for a wonderful shade for weary tourists. The fort is huge and takes a good amount of time to cover up. It holds many still intact water tanks, a huge lake, few palaces and gateways. It does succeed in reminding you of the glorious past.

Back to the base,  we started for Pune. Had a light lunch at a roadside hotel on the way. Were back to the city by 6pm.

Every time I return from a trek and the next day arrives, I always feel rejuvenated, the feeling is of having hit the reset button on all the unnecessary clutter created in life. Makes me reiterate a quote I found on this blog. http://www.scoopwhoop.com/inothernews/travel-changes-you/

With every trip you take, you become just a little wiser.

item.title: The art of programming
item.description: Software development might be a science but an excellent code is a work of art. The programmer uses a language to write code, which has its own grammar. item.content:encoded:
Software development might be a science but an excellent code is a work of art. The programmer uses a language to write code, which has its own grammar. The programmer follows the syntax, composes accurate expressions and does his best to create concise code. As with literature only mere combination of right words and sentences does not produce a beautiful poem or prose, similarly just an act of writing correct code does not make it aesthetic or pleasing. 

Although written to achieve an objective, program itself is a subjective entity. The code is a reflection of the programmers’ personality. Good programmers get emotionally involved with their code, programs are often described using words like ugly, beautiful, awesome or sexy. There is a kind of personal bond with the piece of code. Names of movies, movie characters, ice-creams, donuts, birds, animals, trees, flowers and many other day to day nouns are commonly found as names of software. Programmers are very close to these things from real life and hence they choose to name their software after them. A good programmer relies greatly on intuition rather than memory.

Programming seeks to create a two way interaction, which is a step up from traditional art forms. The users can not only appreciate the beauty of the end result but also play with it. Like an artist programmer derives inspiration from his surroundings and seeks to imitate them. It’s the same reason why today’s interfaces are so more intuitive and quick to learn. People can easily understand the purpose of an object by merely looking at it. It’s no surprise why we have terms like bins, folders, files, note-pads, forms, buttons, drag & drop, click, tap, swipe, eBooks, calendars, drawers and many more used commonly in interface design.

Like atoms in the real world, pixel is the building block of life on screen. Screen gives life to the character. We can program feelings of pain, sorrow, misery by way of pixel manipulation. Almost every real world phenomenon can be simulated in software environment. So be it the universe, solar system, the gravity or the sub-atomic world. Off course we cannot create or impart consciousness to our characters from the virtual world, even if we build physical robots that still doesn’t seem to be the possibility. But with programming we can come unbelievably close to creating the illusion of reality, which at times isn’t illusion at all. Try playing a game like Prince of Persia or Counter strike and see how you respond to the character’s action. Programming gives you the ability to play the role of the creator where your imaginations have no bounds.

If one could learn his spoken language, then the person can learn a programming language too. Like any other language it takes practice and frequent use. Children benefit greatly from learning to program. Programming opens up a whole new world for these kids. For adults there is more than enough in the programming world to provide you with a hobby for a lifetime, whose benefits are incalculable.

item.title: Where is my weekend?
item.description: Currently there is an epidemic that has gripped the IT industry. The epidemic called weekend working. The disease that has left thousands stressful, depressed and unhappy. item.content:encoded:
Currently there is an epidemic that has gripped the IT industry. The epidemic called weekend working. The disease that has left thousands stressful, depressed and unhappy. There is a huge number of smart, hardworking individuals who are exposed to this new way of slave labour. People are forced to forgo the desire to bond with their families, people are coerced to give up their priorities in life and focus on only single objective: saving their only job. There are numerous disgruntled employees who prefer countless hours of gossip at their desks instead of few productive hours of actual work. This may not be the case at every organization out there, but potentially it’s ‘THE CASE‘ at every organization. When things go wrong weekend work is the first solution that appears. Nobody thinks it is unethical to take away people’s moral right to get rest and rejuvenate themselves. Managers instill a sense of guilt into the minds of employees from the very beginning of the project, virtually scaring them off with warnings like: “nobody likes to work on a weekend, you guys better complete your tasks on time and we will never call you over the weekend”. So if at all people are required to work weekends, it’s their own fault as they did not give proper attention to the manager’s prophecy.

Yes I agree, there might be a critical situation where weekend work is the only solution. But if not defined within legal framework or as a matter of policy, then the critical situation becomes a matter of perspective. A weak project manager who is easily scared by the client will turn almost any adversity into a critical matter. I have seen people work weekends at almost all phases of software development. The criticality of the situation is almost always overblown. Weekend work is an easy excuse of the offshore managers for their incompetency. It gives them an argument that says “I am getting my team to work 10-11 hours a day, I am getting them to work over weekends. What more do you expect of me. Things are difficult here, there is very little that is in my hands.” The managers themselves are typical victims of this viciousness. There is no tyranny here, everyone suffers equally. Be it the manager or the employee. The manager’s have to save their job too. The higher management cares very little, they often think people down the hierarchy are usually lazy and do not understand the gravity of the situation. There is wrong sense of pride in upper management who firmly believe that it’s their interfacing with the client that brings million dollar projects, and it’s the job of managers and developers to complete the project in stipulated time, let whatever be the difficulty. I totally agree with the first part, but it’s the second part that bothers me. Let whatever be the difficulty! This thinking has given rise to a sort of moral degradation which eventually results in forcing people to work for 2-3 weeks without a day of rest.

I classify the IT working population into 5 categories based on their likeliness to agree over working a weekend.

  1. Freshers (New joinees)
  2.  People with vested interest (onsite deputation, promotions, good grades)
  3. The gullible, people who cannot say no to authority.
  4. The responsible (Married, debt ridden etc.)
  5. Free spirits. (The I don’t give a damn types)

The responsible and the free spirits are the only ones who oppose the system of weekend work. The rest are either confused or leave it for others to fight, they are okay either ways. It’s a classic psychology game. If anyone agrees to work over a weekend, then the managers use their example to coerce others. If a junior agrees then a senior is obliged as a sense of responsibility. If a senior agrees then junior has to agree as who knows better than a senior. Managers are pretty good at this game. Few who oppose cannot do so forever as they start suffering from cognitive dissonance, Their rational minds asks them to change their opinion by giving reasons of responsibility, obligation, guilt, team work and what not. It’s really difficult to take a stand that you won’t work under unethical conditions when all about you have given up. The major blame for weekend work culture lies on the individuals, who are either too naive to think about their own well-being or are to messed up in the responsibilities of the life. Either way we don’t understand, what constitutes a good work ethic. Nobody talks about weekend work as a matter of right and wrong but instead confuse it with unwarranted situation.

The strong motive for writing this article comes from the psychological and physical impact weekend work has on the minds of the employees.

  1. Weekend work sends a message into the subconscious of individuals that their life is not in their control, they are overworked, and do not have time for simple pleasures of life. Sometimes even though they have plenty of time, they cannot muster up enough energy to get rid of the inertia created by those senseless visits to the office for no reason.
  2. People who work weekends rarely do any kind of physical activity during those times. As such people prefer not to workout even when their lives are okay. Weekend workers don’t feel guilty for abusing their body since they feel trapped and lost. The thought of exercise appears ridiculous compared to the ordeal one is facing. Thus they compromise their health, which might lead to serious disease in near foreseeable future.
  3. People become absolutely inefficient and notoriously gossipy at work. I will bet more time is spent on gossip than actual work. That’s the only creative haven they can resort to and employees use it in all perfection to get rid of their daily stress.
  4. There is a change in attitude weekend work instils a strong dislike towards the organization, superiors and in lots of cases dislike towards the work which is a major blow to person’s individual growth.
  5. Family life is disturbed. People cannot take time off to take care of their loved ones. There are cases where people get called from hospitals, when their loved ones are in intensive care. There are plenty of examples where newly married couples have had the worst times of their life when their marriage just got started.
  6. While you work on weekends there are no plans, no recreational leaves, you are no more master of your life. The very tenets of freedom are killed right there. And nobody makes any fuss about it.

Like many of my colleagues I am not aware of labour laws. Did a bit of googling, but couldn’t find laws that address this hairy issue.
Companies provide an alternative week off by way of their policies towards a weekend worked. But that’s not right as people volunteer (although not true 😛 ) to give up their time of comfort, in order to address the difficult times the project is facing. So they should be paid in a better fashion. The irresponsible company in one case doesn’t even manage the transportation of the employee, and the individual has to cough up his own money to work over weekends, which is more humiliating. Besides thrifty remuneration, the week off itself isn’t any good. I have seen people accumulate week offs to the count of 12-15 in a span of 4 months. Which is a half of their total weekends during that duration. In those times they do not get to enjoy their own paid leaves or public holidays even. There is a blatant abuse of law. People have worked on national holidays and Labor Day at times. What’s more concerning is that the employee accumulates all these leaves which he cannot take and they eventually lapse off, unless off course somebody is allowed to take a big long vacation, which again is a rare case.

Some people may prefer good remuneration for working over weekends or working extra hours at office, as is the case in developed countries. But if you ask me I will say it’s a slice of your precious life that you offer for nothing. Our jobs are means to an end, in case they are not what we wanted them to be. But our time away from that place of work is our opportunity to be better family members, better citizens, better intellectuals and better friends. It’s that time of leisure which makes us more interesting person, if we are missing on that then what life are we leading?

item.content:encoded:
Regular exercise and ability to do heavy physical activity whenever required wasn’t enough to keep away that excess fat around my belly. My diet is moderately regulated, but sometimes it just goes berserk, chocolates and sweets are my greatest adversaries when it comes to losing weight. A hundred times I had tried dieting and failed. It’s not that dieting never worked, but the thing was I had such great expectations, that I was stubborn to have it all or nothing. So whenever I hit a plateau I just quit. Recently it became so worse that I just quit the effort of keeping my weight under check. And as expected this had a dire effect. With weeks and months passing by my weight kept on mounting. The weight that fluctuated between 68-70kg, was now 73 and it didn’t feel right. 

Back from a trip to Goa, I was quite pumped up to lose that extra flab and feel good about myself. Received some very useful tips from my close friends and felt the time was right to just do it. Below is my journey of four weeks that helped me lose more than 10 pounds about 5kg to be more exact. The only thing different this time was that I had better tools, better control and better knowledge of my situation.

Week 1
First week is usually neutral. There is enough will power in reserve, and although body and mind provides a good deal of resistance the will power counter balances it.

Diet:
Breakfast: 1 raw egg, oatmeal, green tea.
Lunch: 1/2 chicken tandoori or sprout-vegetable salad.
Eve-snacks: omelette with brown bread
Dinner: sprout salad

Supplements : 1 vitamin-mineral capsule (Revital) after dinner.

Workout:
Body weight exercises in the morning, with focus on upper and lower body on alternate days.
20-30min walk after dinner.

Lifestyle changes:
Meditation 10min, morning and evening.
A good 8 hour sleep.

Challenges:
Convincing friends, colleagues, family of my intentions, and confronting the ensuing embarrassment. There is not a soul in the world except for you who thinks dieting would be successful.
Weekends normally ruin your resolve, I chose to stay vigilant. I exercised moderately on weekends to remind myself of the goal ahead.

Week 2
I could already see changes happening, I did feel lighter. Overall lethargy of the body was reduced to a great extent. Muscles felt more in control. The Monday felt awesome.

Diet changes:
Eve-snacks: omelette was replaced with no-sugar fruit juice. I freaked over omelette being fried & oily, thus me consuming more than necessary calories.
Dinner: 2 spoon Apple cider juice before sleep, apple cider is known for reducing obesity, I thought of giving it a try.

Workout changes:
Swimming after office hours for about half an hour.

Lifestyle changes:
Meditation 15min, morning and evening.

Challenges:
Avoiding those innocent moments where someone offers you a chocolate or a pastry or some other sweet. Sometimes I felt I was being too conscious, but it helped. I didn’t fall prey. I knew I wouldn’t last for long if this continued, but I wanted to fight it out as long as I could.

Week 3
The weight had reduced considerably. However I felt very low on my overall energy level. It was becoming increasingly difficult to improve my strength training routine. I always felt short of inspiration and energy. Also I had hit the plateau, most visible fat had reduced and it was difficult to spot improvement by just looking at the mirror. The week was long and arduous. However the results were incredible. By the weeks’ end I had made a considerable progress.

Diet changes:
Eating nuts almonds/walnuts whenever possible throughout the day.
Eve-snacks: eating almonds, no fruit juice.
Dinner: 2 spoon peanut butter with sprouts.

Workout changes:
Daily walk of 30min after dinner.

Lifestyle changes:
Meditation 20min, morning and evening.

Challenges:
I was considered for a serious project work which demanded more time, and more focused work. This new task drained a lot of vital energy and I felt exhausted on almost all days. Sometimes I would straight away go to sleep after coming from office so that I didn’t indulge myself on happy food due to lack of energy. Once I had a nice nap of about 20-30 min. I would wake up and go about the tasks remaining for the day.

Week 4
I knew very well that my diet has to end, and it should end on a happy note. I shouldn’t regret it being broken. There shouldn’t be any feeling of guilt when it broke. So I had to gradually switch to eating normal. Also indulge at times but with total awareness of where I was headed to. This week I was merrier as I felt privileged to try stuff that was forbidden for 3 weeks. Now I could observe myself being conscious all the time about whatever went inside my stomach. I was polite in refusing, whenever some delicacy was given due indulgence and it was time to stop.

Diet changes:
Breakfast: 1 raw egg, oatmeal, green tea, with freedom to try any other on alternate days.
Lunch: 1/2 chicken tandoori or sprout-vegetable salad or any other meal that is just about enough and did not make me feel bloated.
Eve-snacks: omelette with brown bread
Dinner: normal meal, no rice.

Workout changes:
Strength training in morning, brisk walk in the evening.

Lifestyle changes:
Meditation 10min, morning and evening.

Closing note:
Dieting is challenging stuff, but we should aspire to see the change in ourselves. Everyone’s body type is unique and experimentation is the key. Experiment, observe and make changes, repeat this process for as long as is possible until you are sure what works best for you. It’s a wonderful feeling when you are lighter, when the clothes just fit and don’t make any effort to contain the body within. Overall it requires one to change the entire routine one follows and be absolutely religious about it. I would confess I didn’t adhere 100% to what I had planned but 100% was always the goal, so don’t feel disheartened if you fail at some time, but make sure you learn from it. The goal should be 100% effort always. Health is a lifelong habit, so make amendments to your life such that they stick with your forever. Get in the habit of reading good articles and research related to wellbeing. Learn yoga and meditation, they will be your guiding light for the days to come.

item.title: Atheism 2.0
item.description: I always preferred being called an agnostic. Although I don’t buy any philosophy that religions profess, I quite didn’t appreciate being called an atheist. item.content:encoded:
I always preferred being called an agnostic. Although I don’t buy any philosophy that religions profess, I quite didn’t appreciate being called an atheist. Atheism somehow meant vanity for me. There is so much that we do not know about our own nature and the nature of the universe that surrounds us. We are deceived by our senses and brain perceptions at almost every stage of life and yet how can we be absolutely certain about our faith. It was this dilemma that kept me from calling myself an atheist. I was open to all the convincing arguments put forward by religions so that I could switch sides with them, but somehow luckily for me that never happened. As I learnt more about religion, the more I distanced myself from it. 

Almost all religions began with exceptional individuals who had extraordinary experiences in their lives. Be it Buddha, Moses, Jesus, Mohammed or saints and sages of the ancient India and abroad. But if we are to consider current research in neuroscience these supposed godly experiences of all these extraordinary men would be simulated in a laboratory in a near foreseeable future. All god experiences are nothing more than psychosomatic experiences and there is enough science literature to back it. If we are to go by statistics alone 99.9% of world population has never had a god experience, but still finds it convenient to believe in one. So yes, if you take pride in belonging to 21st century please don’t buy the hogwash that the religions have to preach.

But there are quite a many wonderful things that I have learnt being associated with religious people. My love for these ways of living makes me a kind of religious man, yet who does not really believe in religion, quite paradoxical 🙂 . So I preferred being an agnostic until now. Although I believe the world will be a better place to live without religion. Although I am sure the general hatred among the masses will exponentially reduce with the death of religion. And although we will have enough time to focus on the ideals of life and principles of morality when religion is removed from our conscience, I somehow cannot guarantee myself the fruitfulness of the endeavor. There are so many things that we would miss if there wasn’t a religion.

Okay! So if I were to just brush aside the idea of religion, there would be so much I will be missing in life. The art of meditation or mindful awareness that I have come to appreciate, where does it stand in absence of religion? The religious congregations where I get to meet so many people whom I cannot meet otherwise, and where the people meet only for the sake of it and not for business, what happens to these communal events in the absence of religion? The grand temples, churches, mosques and other beautiful architectural wonders that are symbols of religions, what significance do they hold in absence of the reason for which they were erected? A filler, a companion in difficult times, what do we have at such times if not god? And so many other aspects of our social and personal life, that are based on religious beliefs and are quite beneficial to our well-being, what would possibly replace them if we cast aside religion. Definitely Atheism can’t replace all of it. If we are to go by current understanding of atheism by the general public, it’s plain boring.

We need to revive atheism. We need to make people realize how rewarding it can be, to be secular. And to the rescue comes the man Alain de Botton. He talks about Atheism 2.0 in the below talk and produces a convincing argument.

http://embed.ted.com/talks/lang/en/alain_de_botton_atheism_2_0.html

item.title: Mangalore City
item.description: Sitting in the train door, legs on the stairs, cool night air thrashing against our face. Yes that was the beginning of a wonderful and memorable trip to Mangalore. The berth next to a rickety door in the 2nd AC compartment, and the constant creaking noise of the door opening and closing couldn’t really dampen…
item.content:encoded:
Sitting in the train door, legs on the stairs, cool night air thrashing against our face. Yes that was the beginning of a wonderful and memorable trip to Mangalore. The berth next to a rickety door in the 2nd AC compartment, and the constant creaking noise of the door opening and closing couldn’t really dampen my spirits. Me and my friend Abhinav reached the station early morning next day for a pleasant surprise called the city of Mangalore. 

Our friend Shrinivas was already at the station with his overworked yamaha FZ two wheeler. Seriously the bike demanded a little attention and so did the helmet that he carried. We did a Tripsy (3 people on a two wheeler) from the station to a nearby place where we could catch an auto rikshaw. The auto wala dropped us at Kottara, the place where our beloved friend stays. The place is also home to the Infosys campus in Mangalore city.

It seemed like Shrini had taken quite a time planning this outing of ours. Like a seasoned travel guide he got us ready in no time, and we were down for breakfast. We had a nice Dosa for breakfast and as soon as we were finished, we headed towards a nearby beach. To reach the beach we had to cross a river by ferry and then behold the beautiful beach called Tannirbhavi. Its a wonderful feeling when your mind is empty and cannot go into it’s automatic day dreaming mode. In a new location it constantly keeps gazing, capturing and recapturing every frame, trying to make sense of the new environment. If you happen to be with nature at such times, the feeling is simply of awe and wonderment. We clicked few pictures along the way and really appreciated our time at the sunny beach. Once we were back to the river in order to get back to the city, I couldn’t help and wonder at the guy who was down in the water at the river bank. The people there were trying to build some kind of jetty to create a stopping platform for incoming boats. So the guys on the bank carried sand bags and dumped them in the river. And this guy in the water would dive in, get hold of the dumped sand bag at the river bed and secure it in place. And this continued. I noticed that the work was in progress when we first got down from the ferry, before moving to the beach. And now we were back almost an hour later and still this guy was down in the water working. Wonder where his super strength came from.

Now it was time for some delicious Mangalore fish at Giri Manjas. Shrini had in his itinerary the best place to give us an authentic sea food experience. That seemingly unnoticeable place had its name appear in the National Geographic’s traveller magazine. True to its reputation the food was spicy and delicious. We had King Fish, pomfret, prawns and some other delicacies. Then we moved to another beautiful location where we had sumptuous ice-cream that just quenched all my appetite. All the food we had so far had a quality about it and yet was way cheaper. Compare it with restaurant rates in Pune where I come from, I just felt rich.

The afternoon wasn’t yet over. We moved to the mall called City Center and watched the movie “Frozen”, the movie is mesmerizing, do watch it if you haven’t done already. Poor Shrini though had forgotten his precious glasses and had to see the 3D movie in a whole new dimension, no wonder why he didn’t like it. We strolled around in the mall for some time and then headed back for some beach time. The city is quite small by comparison, so you can reach almost any location from anywhere in less than 15 minutes and as less as 7 rupees. The transport system is efficient and you wouldn’t be frustrated if you decide upon using the public transport alone. I was quite skeptical at first about the privately run transport buses. The buses had no pattern about them which is characteristic of an organized city transport. Windows from most buses were just open metallic frames with no glass. However poor those buses looked, I had absolutely no complaints about the job they did. I was just flying around the city within no time. Mangalore transport system is quite efficient.

From back home now we headed towards a new beach called Panambur. We had the best of our times here. The beach is clean, the sand is beautiful and the sun was setting. A perfect combination for an ultimate beach experience. Abhinav was so impressed he expressed his appreciation something like this; “This is the bested, cleanest, warmest, greatest, awesomest, sexiest beach.” We played a good amount of time in water. And Shrini was again back at our heels marshalling us back home for the next adventure. We were back, had a bath and were ready for some party.

Shrini took us to an awesome pub called The Liquid lounge. The place is famous for its loud rock music, delicious food and an awesome crowd. Few pegs down and we were on a real high. The loud music was becoming more bearable after few drinks 😛 . We went out of our way to go back to the DJ and get him play our favourite songs. This is the place where you can definitely practice your rock singing (shouting) skills. By the time we were done, none of us were in any good shape to do anything seemingly logical. The poor auto rickshaw guy had to repeatedly listen to Abhinav’s newly received knowledge of great Kannada language. Back to the apartment, nothing could keep my eyes open any longer, I just slept.

We woke up early next morning and yes the Delhi election results were being declared, sure the result for 3 other states were also being declared but let’s call it Delhi election results for simplicity. The drama surrounding the election results added to our day’s enjoyment. We started our journey to Udupi in the morning. The plan was to visit Malape beach and St Mary’s Island. We reached Malape beach and took a boat ride to the St. Mary’s Island. A ferry was available but it’s an entirely different experience to travel by boat on an open sea. The Island is straight out of a movie. Although island doesn’t have a sand beach, It has lots of beautiful rocky pools to swim and take amazing pictures. It also has a shell beach. Here you can click anywhere and you have an awesome wallpaper photo in your camera. I don’t have the literary skills required to describe something that beautiful, just see the picture below and make a judgement for yourself. While returning back me and Abhinav got a rare opportunity to seat atop the bow (front part of the boat). It was as good as sitting on the water itself, just a few inches from it, the experience was simply exhilarating. Throughout the day we constantly tapped our smart phones to check the election result update, it was just way to thrilling to miss out. Next we got down at Manipal University on our way back. Strolled around in the famous university campus and returned back to Mangalore.

We had a train to catch at 8:30 pm in the night. So we quickly got back and got ready to have dinner. Shrini wasn’t yet finished with his plan. He had one more surprise in store for us; “Sea Crabs”. He took us to a wonderful restaurant called Village. We just had enough time to quickly order, enjoy the food and catch the train. After enjoying some beer we got lost in a wonderful discussion. The discussion revolved around doing something besides our regular jobs. On the lines of startups. Doing something different, chasing new ideas. The interesting discussion lasted a very very long time. The first time somebody saw the watch we were already missing our train. We called the station and the train was running on time and we were definitely going to miss it as our crab wasn’t ordered yet 🙂 . There was this mixed feeling, that crops up when something does not turn out as per the plan. Me and Abhinav both had office to reach the next day. But the enjoyment of past many hours was so astounding that we were somewhat happy that we missed the train and had more time with us now. The crab was good and we took our own time to finish.

Moved about in the city on Shrini’s bike in the night. Hope he gives it the utmost necessary servicing it requires soon enough. The next morning had an awesome breakfast at an awesome restaurant called “Chutney”. Had our tickets booked for our return journey by a volvo bus and then bade goodbye to Mangalore just before noon.

I loved the city and would like to visit it again. Few things worth mentioning; I didn’t find any bill boards in the city with ugly politicians on them. Mangaloreans do have a sense of aesthetics. I was quite surprised when I observed nobody supervising the theatre exit door when people returned the 3D glasses received before watching the movie. There is no visible language bias in the city and national language is respected well here. If you love travelling please put this city on your list.

All thanks to Shrinivas for such a wonderful journey. He has set the bar high when it comes to being a host. We will make sure you have same amount of fun when you come visit our city.

item.title: 42kms…
item.description: I am quite comfortable running a half marathon, read my post first half marathon on how I got started. So the next adventure in line was off course completing the full marathon. When I made it public that I was participating in a full marathon, it was wonderful to observe peoples reaction. Some believed in…
item.content:encoded:
I am quite comfortable running a half marathon, read my post first half marathon on how I got started. So the next adventure in line was off course completing the full marathon. When I made it public that I was participating in a full marathon, it was wonderful to observe peoples reaction. Some believed in me, encouraged me saying I could do it. Some thought I was joking and I would run only a half marathon if at all I did. And my good friends just noticed me being more crazy than my usual.

To be honest I like running, but I am not a big fan of long arduous practice sessions. More than 10-15 rounds on a 400mtr track almost makes me giddy and is painfully boring. Even if I ran a new route in the city I would run a maximum of 6-7 kilometers. I also tried my best to be consistent, but I failed there too. Critical office project at the time meant more time spent in office and returning home totally exhausted. It was really difficult at times to harness enough will power to get myself wearing those pretty running shoes and start jogging. Whenever I did I knew it wasn’t hard as it seemed, but the beginning is always difficult. Until 3 weeks prior to the marathon, I wasn’t really in best shape to complete a marathon.

I knew I won’t be able to cover a lot of ground within 3 weeks although my work load had considerably gone down and I could really focus on my training. However I wanted to make sure that I did cross that finish line no matter what. One thing I had learnt from my previous experiences in long distance running and endurance trekking was that; you should always take a break whenever your body starts to give a signal that it’s breaking down. If you keep persistent by being foolishly confident of your endurance and will power, the only thing that will happen is, you being exposed to an injury which will most likely stop you from doing anything more. The old wisdom “slow and steady wins the race” does come handy here. So my plan was quite simple, to keep my body in as much optimal state as possible. My practice did not involve any long distance running at all. I had hardly run 5-6kms at a stretch during last 3 weeks of practice. Instead I focused on other areas too, I walked long distances after dinner like 2-3kms. Then I did a good deal of yoga in the morning. Also I completed a strenuous trek one weekend, staying in the sun the entire day, to test how much stress my body could take in.

Prior to the marathon, I happened to get a lot of interesting tips & tricks from an old school friend. He advised me to keep taking fluids throughout the run and always keep a water bottle ready in hand. To pour water at the back of my neck, when it felt hot, so that the coolness will spread to my head and keep my nerve steady. And some more genuine tips which I needn’t specify here. For me the marathon was going to be a tandem of walk and run until I reached the finish line. Although more prepared than ever, 42kms stood like the Mount Everest. I was still unsure if I could reach in one piece to the finish line in less than 6 hours. And like always even during this marathon’s previous night we had hardly 4 hours of sleep.

The run began at 6:40 am. The sun wasn’t up yet, and the weather was cooler. Running along the seaside felt like dream. Since the distance was long, I wasn’t really focused on the distance markers. I hardly looked at any of them. I didn’t put on my iPod as listening to it could have given me a sense of time. It was quite weird, I didn’t want to know the time. I wanted it to pass unnoticed when I kept persistent at my job. I enjoyed running like never before, not trying to hurry at all, not getting myself out of breath, but just smiling and running that’s all.

The enthusiastic Mumbai crowd was by the side on the streets cheering us. The small children raised their hands for HiFi and would feel very happy when the runner touched their hand. I could imagine myself in their place, I could imagine how wonderful I would have felt when a marathoner gave me a HiFi. I was in no hurry, soaking in the atmosphere, listening to every cheer, smiling and enjoying my run continued. I took my first break after reaching the half marathon marker. Stopped for a while, used some ice, stretched a little and then carried on.

Now the sun was making its presence felt. My speed was dropping and I required more walking breaks than before. The enthusiasm had not dropped one little bit, but body glucose level kept dropping and I could sense it. At 35kms I started to get little cramps in my calves while running. I could walk fine, and knew for certain that if I walked the rest of the distance I would easily complete the race in less than 6 hours. A volunteer along the way had offered me a small relief spray. I made a judicious use of the spray. Under no condition I wanted to expose myself to an injury which will cut short my progress in the run. I used plenty of ice. I would put small pieces in my shoes so that the foot muscles felt relaxed. Those muscles were in real pain and wouldn’t soothe by relief spray as it didn’t work on socks. The last 10 kms were long and hard but were in no way difficult.

Slowly and steadily I was nearing the finish line. I realized I could finish the race in under 5 hours, so I picked up the pace along last 2kms. The cramps however kept me from making any considerable progress. When it was about 600mtr before finish, I stopped. I wanted to have a photogenic finish 😛 . Didn’t want to cross the line with the obvious pain and limp. I used the remaining of relief spray to calm the muscles. Walked up 200 more metres and then finally when I could see the distant finish line and the cheering crowd I picked up my space. I ran as hard as I could, ran as if I just started the race, and was there in a flash. Could see the clock now that I saw at the start of the race. The time was back on my mind.

item.content:encoded:
The Wikipedia article on VLC media player says: “VLC is first in the sourceforge.net overall download count and has been downloaded more than 1.3 billion times”. It works on all major operating systems Windows, OS X, Linux, BSD, Solaris, Android, iOS and few more. VLC has around 600,000 Lines of code, VLC uses a lot of external libraries, which are over 3,020,000 lines of code. This is all handwritten code, work of a decade long programming cycle. The software is available in 48 languages. And needless to say integral part of our virtual lives.

So now coming back to the title of the post, yes VLC media player is a free, open-source software. People can download and use it the way they want without any restriction. If you are programming types, you can download its source code, modify it, change whatever you want, turn traffic cone into traffic signal and redistribute, no questions would be asked. Most people cannot understand how incredible it is, but I will try to throw some light. Firstly we are really not grateful enough to the open-source community out of shear ignorance of what they do to make our lives better. We do not realize how easier and cheaper our life has become thanks to the accumulated works of these countless programmers around the world.

Every computing device we use today, proprietary or otherwise, either uses open source software or is in some way inspired (copied) from it. A report by the Standish Group (from 2008) states that adoption of open-source software models has resulted in savings of about $60 billion per year to consumers. So how do these software come into being, when nobody is paying the developers who develop it? What inspires these individuals around the world to put in the mind boggling effort that is required to write efficient code? What moral code dictates them to distribute the code just like that and not expect a penny for it?

Answer appears from different directions, for some writing code is a form of art, a sort of poetry that should be shared with one and all. For others it’s a community service, their own way of giving back to the world, remember the $60 billion saving to the consumer. For few its a way of bringing transparency into the world of software industry where companies charge fortunes to their client for nothing. To some it’s a way of creating more secure systems that are tried and tested by everyone around the world and not behind the closed doors of a corporation. Open-source development is a way of getting connected with geniuses around the world and learning from their work. Its a unified world with no boundaries. its a way of life with great sense of work ethic & passion without any sort of discrimination.

The open source community takes Isaac Newton’s words: “I stand on the shoulders of the giants” literally. The code evolves every single day based on the great products built in the past. Every day new libraries are created and a few days later a library that manages these libraries is created. I would not dwell into details of which free software affects you how, that would be overwhelming. The evolving field of software development is driven by community and not some corporate ingenuity. Most solutions to great problems are found on the internet in public forums, it’s more of a collaborative effort. Big companies realise this and they are also making huge contributions to the open-source movement, either with man power or with money.

I really adore the work of people like Richard stallman, Eric.S.Raymond, Bruce Perens and many more who have pioneered the idea of free software. It took some time for industry imbibe this idea of how willingness to share ones work with others will help them manifold, as other’s too will make similar contributions. People go through each other’s code; criticise it, find mistakes with it, most times correct it themselves. Open source development is a vibrant world, where you get to learn on an exponential scale through the mistakes and achievements of others.

This article isn’t intended to draw sympathy towards the work of these dedicated folks. It’s just a reminder to all that, you really haven’t paid for everything that you enjoy today. Please use these words consciously. Like free software developers, countless others in countless other disciplines strive every day selflessly to make this world a better place to live, without expecting much in return. Next time you don’t like a free app on android store please don’t just write “This app sucks!!” in comments. If you don’t like just uninstall it. If at all you want to vent out your frustration be more constructive and write a critical review of the app and explain to the developer why the app sucks. Rate the applications on android that you like, least you can do. If you use torrent seed your torrents, don’t be stingy.

There is no end to where software industry will take us. Human imagination is the limit. Some day with improved computation, continued digitization of historical records, archival of internet blogs & new articles, deep study of social network will lead to an artificial intelligence that can almost mimic an average human mind. We have already heavily dependent on computers for our physical and mental wellbeing, so why not get involved with it. If you cannot learn to code teach your children, it’s not really that difficult and can become a wonderful hobby for a lifetime.

item.description: If you can keep your head when all about you Are losing theirs and blaming it on you, If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you, But make allowance for their doubting too; If you can wait and not be tired by waiting, Or being lied about, don’t deal in lies, Or being…
item.content:encoded:
If you can keep your head when all about you
Are losing theirs and blaming it on you,
If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you,
But make allowance for their doubting too;

If you can wait and not be tired by waiting,
Or being lied about, don’t deal in lies,
Or being hated, don’t give way to hating,
And yet don’t look too good, nor talk too wise:

If you can dream – and not make dreams your master;
If you can think – and not make thoughts your aim;
If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster
And treat those two impostors just the same;

If you can bear to hear the truth you’ve spoken
Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools,
Or watch the things you gave your life to broken,
And stoop and build ’em up with wornout tools:

If you can make one heap of all your winnings
And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss,
And lose, and start again at your beginnings
And never breathe a word about your loss;

If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew
To serve your turn long after they are gone,
And so hold on when there is nothing in you
Except the Will which says to them: ‘Hold on!’

If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue,
Or walk with kings – nor lose the common touch,
If neither foes nor loving friends can hurt you,
If all men count with you, but none too much;

If you can fill the unforgiving minute
With sixty seconds’ worth of distance run –
Yours is the Earth and everything that’s in it,
And – which is more – you’ll be a Man my son!

Rudyard Kipling.

item.title: The Lost Wallet
item.description: Of many dreadful experiences in life, one is of losing your wallet. Losing money is the least of our headaches at such times. The process of getting a brand new Credit/Debit card or a new driving license is almost killing. The thing is, there is not enough care in the world that can ensure your…
item.content:encoded:
Of many dreadful experiences in life, one is of losing your wallet. Losing money is the least of our headaches at such times. The process of getting a brand new Credit/Debit card or a new driving license is almost killing. The thing is, there is not enough care in the world that can ensure your wallet doesn’t get lost. People lose things one way or another, it just happens. There are successful organized gangs that do pick pocketing and are thriving. So yes if luck favors we are quite likely to get pick pocketed.

Once it happened, I was visiting a friend. My wallet was in my back pocket as I rode my bike. There were a few traffic signals on the way, and were quite jam packed. Once I reached my destination, got my bike parked and got ready to move to a small eatery, I involuntarily reached my pocket to check the wallet. And my heart just skipped a bit. There was this sudden sunken filling as if I just lost something irreplaceable. I checked my pocket again knowing well the futility of action. The heart beat was picking up speed like a bolting athlete. And for a moment I was just dazed, lost and empty.

My friend arrived, and a sudden smile appeared on my face out of nowhere. Friends mean so much! I told him what had happened. Every ordeal is a joke when discussed with your buddy and this was no different. At first he was like, I knew it all along, with your careless attitude this was going to happen someday. Any ways tell me what all things you lost. And we started analysing the gravity of the situation. Once the situation was read, first task was to block the ATM cards. We went to the nearest internet cafe, got customer care numbers of the two banks which trusted me with those beautiful plastic cards. I dialed in and requested them to block my cards with immediate effect.

Next we went to a nearby police station to report the matter. We thought far ahead, maybe if my wallet was picked by a criminal who got caught at any point. Then it will be more trouble for me as all sorts of questions like what is your driving license doing with this person? How does this man hold your credit card? Would crop up. If you say it was lost then a question would be asked, where is the police complaint? So we thought it was wise to just lodge a FIR as a proof that my wallet was really lost. I suspected that it was stolen at some damn traffic signal. But when I narrated my story to the police, they came up with standard excuses like not under our jurisdiction etc. to just whisk us away. I didn’t have enough will left in me to fight them anymore, so I just gave up. Although it feels me with remorse as to why I didn’t stand up, it felt most wise at that time to just give it up.

Once such a thing happens, it’s a huge pain to explain to the rest of the world what really happened. You have to repeat the same story a hundred times. As most of us have this flair for spicy conversations we always tend to extrapolate things. But for me huge effort was to remember if I had extrapolated something so that my account of the story wasn’t in conflict with what I had told to someone else. People provide different opinions. Some will provide you with wisdom like, it’s never a good idea to keep your wallet in your back pocket while travelling, or when you are in the crowd. It should always be your front pocket at such times. Some people will say, it’s never correct to put all your money at one place like your wallet, instead it should be spread all over your pockets. Hell! How cumbersome that is, I would prefer losing my wallet again. And then there are parents who will look at you like a policeman looks at a criminal and make you believe that it was all your fault. It was quite funny to observe.

So the news was finally out in the public. Next I had to go to the bank to get some cash out. I was back in ancient times, filling out bank slips. I attempted that forgotten signature again, man I never get it correct the first time. Stood in the long queue, while collecting cash the cashier observed I had not updated my bank book in 2 years and coyly asked me if I had lost my ATM card? A little amused I asked how she guessed? She replied people visit the bank for such small withdrawals only when they can’t use their ATMs. Then I filled up the form for a new ATM and got out. Next went to another bank some kilometers away followed the same dull process and the day was up. When you have a bank work, typically that’s the only work you do in the entire day. Next big headache was getting my driving license back. That was going to be a real pain with FIR and all required. So I decided to just postpone the activity for time being.

Just 3 days later when I returned home from my office I saw an unusual package lying on the table. The envelope of the package was made out of notebook paper. A few pages from an old notebook must have been torn to make it. The package was sent by speed post and had the postage seal on it. I could make out the place from where the package was sent by looking at the postal seal. It was a place nearby to where I parked my bike on the day I lost my wallet. On the envelope there was my name and address handwritten in big letters. I quickly opened the package and the sight just blew my mind. There emerged my beautiful wallet in perfect condition. I have not enough words to express my amazement and joy. In the envelope there was also a note, which I opened and began reading.

The note read. Dear Mr. Ajay, you dropped your wallet at a traffic signal last night. I picked it up and searched through it to see if I could find your number. When I couldn’t find it, I used the details on your driving license to find you on Facebook. However I could not find you on Facebook. So finally I decided to post it back to you on the mentioned address. Please make sure you take good care of your precious belongings next time. I read the letter and reread it few more times. It meant a lot. There wasn’t a mention of the sender anywhere on or inside the package. It doesn’t really matter, I will remember the person for the rest of my life.

The package left me with lots of lessons to be followed over a lifetime. My own happiness and joy was a proof enough to do something good in life and not desire to see its impact directly. If you are doing good it will always bring a smile to someone somewhere, you don’t really need to see it. The world is not really bad as we perceive it, it’s just that our eyes are not wide open to see those beautiful people with their wonderful hearts making a difference day in day out.

item.content:encoded:
Grit is passion and perseverance for very long term goals. Grit is having stamina. Grit is sticking with your future, day in, day out, not just for the week, not just for the month, but for years and working very hard to make that future a reality. Grit is living life like it’s a marathon, not a sprint!
Excerpt from the talk on TED by Angela Duckworth.

https://embed.ted.com/talks/angela_lee_duckworth_the_key_to_success_grit.html

There is a lot of research happening currently around the psychological trait ‘Grit’. Most people will claim that they know what grit means but it’s not an easy task to develop it. Actually I feel the other way, it’s the ignorance of our own nature that stops us from becoming grittier. If we look back at our lives, there are some things we are good at today because we have worked on them for very long, maybe months, years or perhaps decades. A small child learning to walk, climb, talk is the best example of grit. Those skills aren’t just mastered suddenly, the muscles develop over time and the child keeps trying. The way children learn how to read and write is again an example of grit. Learning alphabets is just too much work for a small child, but as the time goes, with repeated application and persistent effort the child becomes better at it and if the effort continues forever she might become a good prose writer someday. The same goes for any other skill.

So the bottom line is this. If we really wish to develop a new skill, we should not quit let happen what. We might fail, we might give up for some time, but come what may we should come back and start over again. Just give that skill enough time to flourish. Think of it as an insurance policy that would mature in a long foreseeable future. If a good health is your goal, make it a habit to workout at least 5min every day. Whenever you feel more motivated put in more effort, but 5min. should be your everyday target no matter what. Trust me it will improve your physique like it never did. Grit is not the perfection of a discipline but a process of building up a discipline with sincere effort. We would fail like we always do, we might lose touch for some time, we might give up but if we really want to achieve we will come back to it again and again and never stop.

The topic of Grit is worth a post because if one can understand its role in fulfilment of one’s goal, one can truly achieve it. Please note though grit is useful only when used in action not in thought. Thinking about mastering a particular programming language over a course of 1 year won’t make you any good at it. Instead, writing few lines of code every single day in the same language and giving some 10min. reading time to its documentation will surely make you a master in no time.

item.title: Sing, Smile and do Service
item.description: What do we really want in life? item.content:encoded:
What do we really want in life? The spiritualist, the philosopher, the psychologist, the school or college teacher, the affectionate father or a wise elder, all will give you their version of what it means to live. The problem is that none of these answers, however wise they seem really resolve the question. For that question itself is life. Think about it; this profound question: what do I really want in life? Is all that is there to life? At times it seems like we do know the answer, but we keep coming back to the question, whatever be our age. It gives us a sense of purpose, a vision of destiny. 

Life is very dynamic, although we try and believe that everything is linked and there is an underlying order. Deep down we do know that work life can be surprising, painful at times. Many have tried simplifying this randomness of events in life through different ideas. For some it’s a will of God, they believe this apparent chaos is actually order for the controlling & commanding god. For more intellectual types it might be the work of the subconscious mind or a result of collective consciousness of the societies etc. Whatever it is, it really doesn’t matter life is chaotic.

I am always fascinated by this dynamism of life events. The inherent uncertainty that surrounds us. Not knowing what might happen. Consider the daily traffic that we pass, countless small or big accidents have happened on that route. From my own driving experience I know for sure that our being a good driver or rider is not sufficient enough to insulate ourselves from a freak accident. The robbery next door in the same apartment, could have happened at our house also. There are so many evil things that happen to innocent people all the time; that sucks! But life works that way. Off course I should take into consideration the beautiful surprises too that happen along the way. A surprise visit by close friends. A sudden wonderful job opportunity that we never dreamed of, or a very rare lottery etc.

However for untrained minds this randomness is too much. So some rely on religion and believe that their worship will in some way keep them safe and sound. Some Non-believers will confront this randomness of events with a nihilistic idea that there isn’t much too the life any ways. The inquisitive will tackle it with their constant search to find meaning. For me any of this approach is just fine. But none of them make life fun at all. The wisdom that I share below is borrowed from core principals of an organization called Art Of Living. I happen to be an on-off volunteer associated with it. I really love their efforts at reducing all that unnecessary stress in the world. I summarize what I have learnt in three simple words: Sing, Smile & Service.

Music is an integral part of our life and singing is a great stress buster. You don’t need to be singer to sing. Just take some time to hum yourself a nice tune and see how it makes you a pound lighter, not literally 😛 . So sing by all the means. Some who really don’t like singing, although I don’t see why somebody will hate their own singing voice but still, you can pursue any art that may be more close to your taste. Take up some instrument, or start sketching, or start writing. In short just get yourself an interesting hobby that will make life really worth it. This sums up what I really mean by sing; have something in life that is close to your heart and you don’t really expect any material gains from it.

Wear a smile and have friends; wear a scowl and have wrinkles.
George Eliot

That’s exactly what it means. Smile is very integral to our well-being, and it truly makes you look younger. If you are not the smiley types just one suggestion to you as given by my teacher; “fake it, until you make it”. A smile in your life will change you forever, it will make you more empathetic. Yes there are some people who appear all smiley and sugary on the outside but are completely rotten and corrupt, but that’s not my point. You keep smiling starting now and see the world lighten up.

I slept and dreamt that life was joy. I awoke and saw that life was service. I acted and behold, service was joy.
Rabindranath Tagore

Service is most ignored aspect of our life. People find gazillion reasons as to why they can’t do service. For some service only means joining a NGO or some sort of volunteering. Service can be performed anywhere any time. Just be compassionate and have a simple thought. How can I make someone’s day a little easier? From the time you wake up until you sleep, you will get more than a dozen opportunities to help someone. And dozen is just a smallish estimate, you will get many more opportunities if service is a habit for you. Well how does it help you? It’s quite simple, service makes you lose yourself, and your consciousness expands. If I were a neuro-scientist I could tell you exactly what areas in your brain lighten up and which hormone get secreted, but you get the point. It makes you feel awesome. And don’t forget to hold the smile.

Just to summarize, remember to Sing, Smile & do Service. Be absolutely selfish about it. It has made my life much easier and might make yours too 🙂 . And all that life’s randomness, trust me it won’t bother you. You will show poise when in pain by smiling, you will relieve pain through your service and embrace the unknown through your singing.

item.title: Movies to fuel your imagination
item.description: Below is the list of movies that really change perspective. They are the great examples of how best our imagination can work. I haven’t put them any particular order, but just listed them.
item.content:encoded:
Below is the list of movies that really change perspective. They are the great examples of how best our imagination can work. I haven’t put them any particular order, but just listed them. 

Back to the future​

I have never been able to understand the concept of time travel. Even the book brief history of time by Stephen Hawking hasn’t helped much. However this movie makes time travel absolute fun. It’s pure classic humor, a must watch!

Batman (Dark Knight) Series​

Christopher Nolan is commercially most successful director and Dark Knight trilogy is the main reason. These movies are intense, thought provoking. An Incorruptible hero (Batman) is an awesome concept. The movies cover all aspects of our emotions. Love, hate, hope, despair, greed, determination.

Star Wars​

A movie series that fueled the imagination of a generation. Star war movies inspired research into space & technology. The make of this series is a legendary tale. If you wish to know what creativity is then watch star wars from beginning to end.

Harry Potter​

In a way my generation grew up with Harry Potter. The book is very close to our heart. For a moment I would dream of escaping into the new world of endless possibilities and magic. The movie series is lovely. Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, is an amazing watch.

Jurassic Park​

Science proved that the giant dinosaurs did exist on the planet and perished due to some reason. Some guy thought hmm what would have been a world like if dinosaurs did exist, and we have to live with them. I bet you if you haven’t seen the movie – you won’t be able to imagine even 0.01% of what’s shown in the movie. The series is phenomenal.

X-men​

One movie where mutation becomes interesting. Guys with special powers. Clashing ideologies. A scared government. X-men is all about style. The concept is awesome and you will enjoy every part. You just can’t miss wolverine.

Matrix​

One movie I never stop talking about. The theme is open to wide array of interpretation. Just like in matrix our minds are conditioned, the moment we realize this we are on a road to freedom. The movie has lot to teach. More so there are awesome fight sequences, cool sunglasses, martial arts. Beautiful blend of art and science.

Indiana Jones​

For those interested in mythology, occult, archeology, history and a hero-villain story this is a must watch series. Harrison ford makes full justice to the demanding role. The movie series is full of surprise, humor and interesting things.

Pirates of the Caribbean​

Nothing to be said here. Jack sparrow simply rocks. To think on such a imaginative scale the director must have really visited a madhouse. The movie series is biggest ambassador of unconventionalism. It’s an absolutely new world, a world never imagined.

Transformers​

Cars turning into Robots, I mean even if you can imagine this stuff. How do you show it. The fight sequences in transformers are unbelievably detailed. Makes me wonder, how do these animators keep track of what component of these machines should move at what time when the super fast fights begin.

Lord of the Rings​

Kept the best one for the last. Goblins, dwarves, A wizard, hobbits, kings, sorcerers, elves lord of the rings is an inspired creation. The details are awesome. The Middle Earth concept seems so real. Beautiful, breath taking landscapes. Perfect fight sequences. There is enough in the series to keep you interested for eternity.
